name: Orana 44 – New Engines
why: Privately owned, never chartered, EU-VAT paid; new 2025 Beta 40hp engines + new saildrives (~300h, 5-year warranty), new 2025 main, 2,000W solar, 900Ah LiFePO4, Victron, generator, 60 L/h watermaker, full A/C + heat, radar/AIS, two independent autopilots, Coppercoat.
risks: Standing rig replacement date is not disclosed—only a full rig check June 2026; genoa age unclear; 2022 survey is old; 4-cabin layout despite 'owner' wording; verify generator hours, lithium installation/brand and structural/moisture history.
next_step: Request 2022 survey, June 2026 rig report, standing-rig age/chainplate history, generator hours/service, battery invoices/diagram, Beta warranty transfer, moisture/repair history.
notes: Possibly the best new value find: Caribbean geography + new propulsion + serious off-grid system at a sub-€300k ask.

name: Island Time
why: Full 2024 Yanmar/SD60 repower by Just Cats; mast/rig overhaul; professionally installed 10×100Ah Dragonfly lithium bank, 1,920W SunPower solar, Victron 3kW/120A system, watermaker and efficient Frigomar A/C. Owner reports weeks off-grid and only a few hundred generator hours over three seasons.
risks: Need actual Just Cats/Yanmar/rig invoices and survey; ~940/1,050h replacement engines; sail ages still need documentation; ex-Moorings Belize hull. A/C figures are owner estimates rather than logged overnight testing, though the system design and operating history are credible.
next_step: YOUR DECISION: choose whether to schedule the owner call. Before any travel, obtain the promised Just Cats/Yanmar/rig invoices and survey. No response sent.
notes: New owner power memo: 10×100Ah Dragonfly lithium with copper bus bars; 1,920W solar on two primary MPPTs plus a spare MPPT; 3kW MultiPlus. One A/C night-mode scenario is estimated at ~300Ah for six hours, replenished in ~3.5–4 sunny hours.

name: Kostenfalle
why: Major documented 2021 cruising refit replaced engines + saildrives (Volvo D2-75, ~900h), standing/running rig, 1,200Ah lithium, ~1.65kW solar and dual Victron 3kVA; also 10kVA Fischer Panda, 40 GPH watermaker, Starlink/networking, 2025 crossbeam/windows and 2026 genoa. Seller has now supplied a 2021 survey and a large receipt stack, materially improving provenance.
risks: Older 2007 ex-charter hull and 4-cabin layout; 2021 lithium is now ~5 years old; no current survey or oil analysis; owners never actually tested overnight A/C from batteries, so that capability remains theoretical. Saildrive diaphragm/shaft-seal replacement date and the exact reason for the 2025 crossbeam replacement are still open, and current structural/moisture condition needs a fresh survey.
stage: Diligence active — seller records received; narrow follow-up sent
next_step: Wait for the saildrive diaphragm/seal date and explanation for the 2025 crossbeam replacement; review the 2021 survey/receipts. Then Max decides whether the documentation and broker-indicated ~10–12% negotiating range justify a fresh survey/showing. No call or travel has been requested.
notes: Seller says the refit was driven by 13 years of Caribbean use and traces of water in the original engine/saildrive oil, not a disclosed casualty. No known damage disclosures. Fischer Panda was bought used at 2,637.6h after authorized service and is believed only a little over 2,700h now. Lithium shows no observed degradation. Broker expects a clean deal to land within roughly 10–12% of ask. Technical follow-up sent 9/3 only for seals and crossbeam cause.

name: Private Seller Lagoon 450

risks: ~5,500h engines; private-sale verification required; survey findings may change ranking materially.
next_step: Seller says documents were sent, but none reached Gmail yet; our reply to Boat Trader notification bounced. Reconnect through Boat Trader Messages and obtain survey/oil analysis.

name: Bound for Freedom
why: Never chartered owner version with 2026 1,680Ah LiFePO4, 1,900W solar, Victron, 30 GPH watermaker, 2024 main, 2025 saildrive seals/rudder bearings, 2024 Coppercoat, radar/AIS, Starlink, extra refrigeration and extensive spares. Broker says the new lithium system was designed with a future A/C installation in mind.
risks: No generator or installed A/C; replacement jib is quoted around $6k; standing rigging was inspected/tuned in 2025 but replacement date is still not stated. Vessel has not been imported into the USA and broker says current tariffs make importation expensive, so the US-buyer transaction path remains a material cost/legal diligence item.
stage: Broker supplied A/C quote + partial facts — call requested
next_step: YOUR DECISION: whether to take Caroline's call. No reply or call was scheduled automatically. If proceeding, use the call to unlock the remaining records, standing-rig report/survey details, exact import/tariff transaction structure and seller flexibility.
notes: Broker supplied A/C quote/specs, says there is no known material damage or hurricane history and that the boat spent most of its life in the Mediterranean. She wants a buyer conversation before spending hours redacting additional records. This is now a true buyer-next-step gate rather than an unanswered-email problem.

name: Lexak
why: ~20kWh lithium architecture, ~3.1kW solar, 2026 standing rigging, newer sails, reinforced/certified bulkheads, strong off-grid fit.
risks: Former charter; ~3,500h engines; generator reported around 11,000h is a major diligence item.
next_step: Confirm generator rebuild/replacement plan, charter/hull-repair history, battery architecture, survey/moisture report.

name: Pivot
why: Major cruising refit: 1,320Ah lithium (2022), 2.25kW solar, 5kW Quattro, 70 GPH watermaker, Starlink/Iridium, backup autopilot, newer rig/sails, extensive mechanical work and documented bulkhead reinforcement. Broker supplied a December 2025 condition survey and supporting file stack.
risks: Bulkhead work was symptom-driven after doors became difficult to close. The Dec. 2025 survey also flagged forward-crossbeam corrosion/paint blistering and a large starboard-foredeck crack. Broker now says the foredeck crack was repaired/repainted by a local fiberglass worker paid in cash, with no invoice, and the crossbeam was DIY sanded/repainted after a rigging company characterized the corrosion as surface-level. Those repairs are not independently documented. Onan has 10,320h; ~3,900–4,100h engines; 51-ft ownership-cost penalty; prior survey was dockside only.
stage: Diligence active — repairs verbally confirmed; independent verification required
next_step: YOUR DECISION: whether to use Brandon/Peter's offered video inspection or consider a survey-contingent offer. No call/offer initiated. Before travel or commitment, require an independent pre-purchase haulout/survey with direct scrutiny of the foredeck repair, crossbeam and bulkhead work.
notes: Brandon offers to have Peter Hoff of Dutch Yacht Services walk the repaired areas and bulkhead work on video. Transparency is a positive, but the cash/DIY repair documentation remains materially weaker than invoices/photos and does not replace an independent survey.
